# git it problem

Fix `git it` with a combined date offset:

```
$ git it -191d10H root
Reinitialized existing Git repository in /Users/.../Development/public/kamilsk/observer/.git/
-191d10H: Cannot apply date adjustment
usage: date [-jnRu] [-d dst] [-r seconds] [-t west] [-v[+|-]val[ymwdHMS]] ... 
            [-f fmt date | [[[mm]dd]HH]MM[[cc]yy][.ss]] [+format]
fatal: invalid date format:
```

BSD `date` takes one unit per `-v` flag; the offset reached it as a single `-v-191d10H` adjustment and was rejected, so the timestamp came back empty and the commit failed with `invalid date format`. `git init` had already run (harmlessly, on an existing repository).

Expected: `-191d10H` is split into `-v-191d -v-10H`; `git it` either commits with the shifted date or fails before touching the repository.

See the note on #30: `git init` still precedes the date computation, so a `datetime` failure leaves a half-done init. Unit letters are BSD-specific (`H`,`M`), so the sketch's lowercase `h`/`m` would still fail.
